description: Scenes with a purpose (owner, Oct 15, evening): the narrator's setup, the asker's opening and statement of purpose, the player's four replies with their stakes, the asker's answer and the close. Authored to calibrated patterns from ordinary American political and family talk (the text rule, Oct 15); no one's text is copied. Each piece serves every scene with its step and move: each use names the purpose it serves, so a line never leaks into a scene it does not fit; a follow that answers one reply names that reply's piece or move in `after`. A piece's bearing is the manner of its wording; the speaker's traits pull toward the bearings they favor. The director's exchange engine (src/director/scene-talk.ts) arranges the pieces by src/director/data/purpose-arcs.json.

parts.text: Is there something you wish somebody had asked you a long time ago?

parts.text: Honestly, a regular life with some use in it. Dinner with people I like, and one thing I fixed that stayed fixed.

parts.text: I got here by saying yes to small things. One led to another, and I'm still not sure when it got serious.

parts.text: I'd like to be useful without being noticed for it. That's harder than it sounds.

parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Thank you for sitting through my nerves. You were kind about it.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: I'd like to do this again. I'll ask you properly, no circling the block first.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Next time I'll bring the questions I was too nervous to ask. Fair warning.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Okay, go on, I get it. I'm glad you came, and if you want to try again, I'd like that.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: That's all right. I enjoyed what we got to. Ask me again whenever you want.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: The lease renewal sits on the table between your mugs. {name} hasn't touched it, and hasn't touched the coffee either.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: You're drying a dish when {name} comes in and stands there with one hand in a pocket, turning something over.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: The bills are sorted into two piles again. {name} sets the pen down and waits until you look up.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: One drawer with both your things in it, and a spare key on the hook. {name} pulls a chair out and sits across from you.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Hey. Got a minute? Leave the dish, it can wait.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Sit with me for a second. Nothing's wrong.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: I've been trying to find a good way to start this, and there isn't one.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Before you pick up the bills again, can I say something?
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: I got a ring. It's in my pocket and my hand is shaking. Will you marry me? You can look at it after you answer.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: We split the rent and argue about the dishwasher. I want to keep doing that for good. Marry me.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: I practiced this and forgot it. So, plainly: I'd like to be your spouse. Will you marry me?
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: I keep writing both our names on everything anyway. I'd like it to be official. Will you marry me?
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: I don't need a big thing. A clerk, two signatures, and the rest of it at this table. Will you marry me?
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Yes. I've been wondering when you'd ask, and I'm glad it's you sitting there asking.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Yes, I'll marry you. Put the ring on me before I start crying into the dishwater.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Yes. I can't think of anyone else I want signing the lease next to me.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Yes. Of course. Give me the ring, and then I'll stop shaking.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: I love you, and I'm not going anywhere. But I'm not ready to marry, and I won't say yes just to make this easier.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: You mean a lot to me. Marriage isn't what I want, and I'd rather tell you straight than let you hope.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: I can't say yes. I'm happy with what we have. I just can't picture the wedding part of it.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Can I ask what's behind this? Did something change, or did you just decide?
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Are we talking about the money side too? Combined accounts, the debts, who's on the lease?
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: How soon are you thinking? I want to know whether you mean a date or just a direction.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: I'm not saying no. I need more time to think. Can you give me that without it being strange between us?
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Ask me again after we've sorted the bills and I've had room to think. I want my answer to be real.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: I wasn't ready for it. Let me sit with it a while, and I'll come to you.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: You said yes. I'm going to need a second. Thank you, really.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Thank you. I was sure you'd laugh, or say something about the ring.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Okay. Good. Thank you for answering straight away. I didn't have to stand here guessing.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Okay. Thanks for telling me straight. It stings, but I'd rather know where you are.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: I hear you. The ring goes back in the drawer, and we're still us. I'll take that.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Alright. I'm not going to push. Thank you for not just saying what I wanted to hear.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Can you at least think about why? If it's the money or the paperwork, we could change that.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Please don't close it for good. Just keep it in mind while we do the bills and the dishes like always.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: I thought we were headed there. Tell me what I got wrong, and I'll listen.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Nothing changed, that's the point. I noticed I'd already planned around you. I wanted to say it out loud.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Yes, the money too. I'd put my name on the lease with yours and open one account. I've got numbers if you want them.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: No date. I'm not in a hurry. I just want to know we're headed the same direction.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: How long, though? I can wait, but I'd like to know whether I'm waiting for a yes or a polite no.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Is it me, or the idea? Tell me which, and I can work with either.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Okay, but I put myself out there. Give me something to hold on to, even if it's small.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Take it. I'd rather have a slow yes than a quick one you regret.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Fair enough. The ring can stay in my pocket. I'll be here when you want to talk.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Alright. I asked, and you're thinking. That's more than I expected, honestly.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Thank you for choosing this with me. We'll work out the rest together, same as the rent.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: I'm glad it's you. Now let me put this ring on you and we'll finish those dishes.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Thanks for saying yes. I'll stop fidgeting and make us some coffee.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Okay. I'm still here, and I still want the same table. Just not this question.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: I understand. Thank you for being honest. I'll put the ring away and we'll go on.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Alright. I'm not leaving over it. I just need a little quiet first.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Go ahead, clear your head. The ring will keep. Come back whenever you want to talk.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Take some air. I'm not going to chase you with the question. Your key's on the hook.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: {name} has been holding the same cup for a long while. You can tell it's gone cold, because {name} hasn't taken a sip since you walked in.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: A few flattened boxes lean against the wall by the door. You didn't put them there. The tape is on the shelf beside them, still in its wrapper.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: {name} sets the phone face down and turns to look at you.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: {name} says your name once, quietly, the way people do when something has already been decided.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Can you sit with me? I'd like to say this while we're both sitting down.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Thanks for coming in. I've been putting this off, and I don't want to keep doing that to either of us.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: I need to tell you something, and I'd like you to let me get all the way through it first.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Hey. Sit down for a minute, would you? It's not about the bills. Well, not only about the bills.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: I'm ending this. I've thought about it for a long time, and I keep landing in the same spot. I don't think we're good for each other anymore.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: I love you. I just don't think that's enough to keep living like this. We've both been lonely in the same place.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: I can't keep pretending it's fine. We stopped really talking a long time ago, and I'm tired of acting like we didn't.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: It's over, and I'm sorry. I'll start looking for a place. The lease has both our names on it, so we'll have to work out how to get out of it.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: I think we want different things, and we've both known it. I'd rather say it plainly than wait until one of us gets bitter.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: What changed? Last I knew we were getting by, or I thought we were. Help me understand when this started for you.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Is there something specific, or is it just everything adding up? I'd like to know what I'm answering to.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Did something happen that I missed? Tell me, even if it's hard to say out loud.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Okay. I think I've felt it too, and I didn't want to be the one to say it. It still hurts to hear.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: I understand. I'm not going to argue you out of it. I just need a minute before I can think about boxes.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Alright. If that's where you are, begging won't help either of us. I'll help work out the rest, but I'm going to be quiet for a bit.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: I hear you. I wish it had gone another way. We did try, and I want to remember that.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: I'm sorry I wasn't paying attention. I let a lot of things slide, and I can see that now.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: I'm sorry for all the times I was somewhere else in my head, even when you asked me to be here.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: I'm sorry. For what I didn't say and for what I said badly. I wish I'd done better by you.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: You've already decided, haven't you? You didn't ask me for anything. You packed boxes first and told me second.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: You sit me down and hand me a finished plan? You could have said something while it still mattered.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: So I'm supposed to be fine with this? I'm the one who stayed and kept trying. Don't tell me it was both of us.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: You got to think it over alone for as long as you wanted, and I get five minutes. That isn't fair, and you know it.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: It wasn't one thing. It was a lot of small ones, and I stopped believing they'd change. I should have told you sooner.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Nothing happened that you missed. That's part of it. I just couldn't picture us any further along than this.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: There's nobody else, if that's what you're asking. I got quieter, and so did you, and neither of us said so.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Thank you for not making this worse. I know it isn't easy to hear.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Thank you. I was afraid you'd hate me, and you're being more decent about this than I expected.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: I appreciate that. You didn't have to take it so calmly, and it means something to me that you did.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: I appreciate you saying that. It doesn't change my mind, but it does help to hear it.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Okay. I'll take that. I have my own share in this too, and I'm sorry for it.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Thank you. I believe you. That's part of what makes this so sad.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Sorry doesn't change what I've decided. I need you to hear that, so you don't hope for something I can't give.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: I know you mean it. But you've said it before and nothing moved. I can't keep waiting to see if this time is different.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: You're right to be angry. I did this badly. But I wouldn't have been honest if I'd waited any longer.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: I know it feels like I ambushed you. I tried to find a way to say it that wouldn't hurt, and there isn't one.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Maybe I did. I was scared you'd talk me back into it, so I got ahead of it. I'm sorry.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Please don't make this a fight. I want to be able to look at you afterward. Can we just get through the practical parts?
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: I'm asking you to stay level with me so we can sort out the lease and the car without it getting ugly.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: I don't want us to end with shouting. Can you give me that much, and let me keep my voice level too?
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Okay. You keep the car, I'll take what's in the boxes, and we'll go through the lease together. That's a start.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Alright. I'll leave my key with you when I go, and we'll pass the paperwork back and forth. Thank you for doing this the hard way with me.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Good. Let's keep it simple and fair. Whoever can't cover the rent alone gets help from the other until the lease is sorted out.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Thank you for hearing all of it. I'll start with the boxes and leave the rest alone until you're ready.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Thank you for staying until I finished. It would have been easier to walk out, and you didn't.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Thank you. Really. I hope we can be decent to each other even after the key gets handed back.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Alright. Go if you need to. The lease and the car will still be here when you want to talk about them.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: Okay. Take your time. I'll be here with the boxes, and we can pick this up when you're ready.
parts.author: Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Lives, night crew)

parts.text: {name} holds out a small wrapped gift and says it is nothing.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: {name} stops by with a gift bag and a smile that has been practiced.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: I won't keep you. I only wanted to bring you something.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: Hope this isn't a bad time.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: It's just a little something. A thank-you for the time you give this place.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: Nothing fancy. There's a gift card in there, dinner on me.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: Open it later, if you like. It's only a thank-you, and I'd like to be remembered kindly.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: Before the vote, I wanted you to have a small thank-you. No strings.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: While the bids are being read, I wanted you to have a small thank-you. No strings.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: That's thoughtful of you. Thank you.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: Alright, I'll take it. Thank you.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: That's kind, but I can't take gifts from anyone with business here.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: Thank you, but keep it. I don't accept anything.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: You didn't need to do that.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: Put it away for now. We can talk later.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: A gift to someone you want something from is a bribe. I'm reporting it.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: I have to get back to work. Take that with you.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: Thank you for stopping by. Take the gift with you.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: I'm glad. Enjoy it.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: Good. I hoped you'd see it that way.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: No, of course. I should have thought. I'll take it back.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: I understand. Forget I came by.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: It's only a gift. Won't you at least look at what's in it?
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: It would mean a lot to me, and it costs you nothing.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: Then keep it for later. It'll be right here when you want it.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: Take it home to your family, then. Nobody's keeping score.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: You don't have to decide now. Just take it with you.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: {name} sets a thick envelope on the table between you and does not sit down.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: {name} has brought more than a gift this time, and the way it is carried says so.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: Close the door, please.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: I'll be direct.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: That's a lot of money, and it's yours. All I need is for the answer to go my way.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: Count it if you like. It's a serious sum, and I want a serious answer.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: I'd like this to be the last time you worry about money. Just see that it goes my way.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: There's real money in this envelope. All I need is your vote when it comes up.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: There's real money in this envelope. All I need is for the contract to come to me.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: Set it down. I'll see that it goes your way.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: Alright. Leave it, and let me handle the rest.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: No. That's far too much for any favor, and I won't be bought.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: Take it back. You can't pay me enough for this.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: That's a serious crime, and you just committed it in front of me. I'm calling it in.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: That's a lot to put on a table. Give me time before I say anything.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: I won't answer today. Take the envelope with you while I think.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: We're finished here. Take your envelope and go.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: Twice the number is still no.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: Now you're raising the offer. I'm reporting both.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: I could make it twice that, if the number is the problem.

parts.text: Name a number. Everyone has one.

parts.text: {name} asks to talk.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: {name} catches you alone, the way a friend does, and asks for a favor.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: Got a minute? It's me.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: I hate to ask, you know that.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: You've always been straight with me, so I'll be straight. I need this to go my way, and there's something in here for you.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: I wouldn't ask anyone else. Take it, and think of it as one friend looking out for another.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: After everything between us, I figured you'd understand. It's only a favor.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: I'd never put this on anyone else. See that your vote goes my way, and take this for your trouble.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: I'd never put this on anyone else. See that the contract comes to me, and take this for your trouble.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: For you, fine. But this stays between us.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: Alright. I trust you not to make me regret this.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: I can't, and you shouldn't have asked. Please put that away.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: Not even for you. Take it back.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: I'm sorry. I care about you, and I can't do this.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: I wish I could help. Not like this, and I'm sorry.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: I thought better of you. This is a bribe, and I'm reporting it, even from you.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: Let me sleep on it. Give me a few days, as a friend.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: I have to go. I'll call you, but not about this.

parts.text: Please. After all the years, you'd really say no?
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: I'd do it for you. You know that.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: You'd report me? After everything?
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: Just think about it. For me.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: Then forget it. I won't ask again, and I'm still your friend.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: I understand. I'd rather you told me the truth than took it.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: No, I'm the one who should be sorry for asking.
parts.author: Story (Claude Code), civic-prose

parts.text: {name} is back with another envelope. You have been here before.

parts.text: {name} has come around a second time, as if the first answer had been a draft.

parts.text: I know. You told me last time.

parts.text: Thank you for answering, {first}.
